From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>

Subject: Post-call recap & proposed POC plan (model selection + success criteria)

Hi Sofia / Tom,

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our discovery and a proposed next step for the POC so we can lock timelines: 

Key goals you shared:
- Replace manual triage for customer inquiries to cut initial response time to < 60s and increase automated resolution rate from 42% -> 75% during trial.
- Support English + Spanish initial triage and summarization for EU/US support queues.
- Keep data residency in US; no customer data to leave your VPC for Private deployment later.

Proposed POC scope (30 days):
1) Baseline evaluation: run your past 2k support threads through candidate models for intent classification, response draft quality, and hallucination rate.
2) Integration test: small integration with your staging Zendesk webhook to validate end-to-end latency and formatting.
3) Multilingual checks: English (en-US) and Spanish (es-ES) prompt sets + evaluation metrics.

Model recommendation for the trial (initial):
- Primary: Mistral-7B-Instruct (quantized on our Dedicated pool) - balance of instruction-following quality and token cost.
- Fallback: Llama-2-13B-chat (higher safety and chat-context retention) - auto-fallback for complex threads or when we hit latency SLOs.

Success criteria (we recommend tracking these during the POC):
- Automated resolution rate >= 65% on the trial dataset (measured vs. your human labels).
- Average generation latency (end-to-end) < 750ms for single-turn responses in staging.
- Spanish NLU F1 >= 0.78 on your annotated set.
- Regression checks: no increase in hallucination rate > 2% compared to baseline.

Ownership & next steps:
- Redwood: set up model endpoints, run baseline batch evaluation, provide evaluation dashboard and per-model cost estimate. (Owner: Marissa Cole)
- Globex: share anonymized sample threads (2k) + Spanish test set and acceptance criteria spreadsheet. (Owner: Sofia Ramos)
- Proposed kickoff: Wed 11/18 at 10:00am PT for technical handoff and timeline alignment.

Attached: draft POC scope PDF and SOC2 questionnaire we asked you to review.

If this all looks good we can send over the MAP and get the kickoff on the calendar.

Cheers,

Ben Carter
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0134

Subject: Re: Post-call recap & proposed POC plan (model selection + success criteria)

Ben / team,

Couple of notes on model selection + evaluation plan from an engineering / runtime perspective: 
- Mistral-7B-Instruct is a strong primary choice for instruction-following and cost; it also handles Spanish reasonably well on our internal fine-tuned prompts. For Mexican + European Spanish differences we recommend including both dialects in the Spanish test set rather than switching models.
- Fallback routing: we typically implement a hybrid approach - confidence threshold (model logit-based score) first, then latency SLO fallback if response time crosses 900ms. We'll also add a simple rule-based override for any threads tagged "legal" or "refund" to always route to the 13B variant.
- Metrics & evaluation plan (30-day POC):
  * Day 0-3: ingest sample dataset and run batch baseline against both candidates.
  * Day 4-10: run A/B runs with Mistral-7B-Instruct vs Llama-2-13B-chat across 1k threads; collect per-case quality scores, latency, and safety flags.
  * Day 11-20: integrate with your staging Zendesk webhook and run end-to-end tests (latency, formatting, ticket triage accuracy).
  * Day 21-30: polish prompts, run final acceptance tests and prepare evaluation report.
- For caching & latency: enable prefix/KV caching for repeated conversational contexts to keep median latency < 600ms in Dedicated.

I'll put together the initial eval script and cost delta table (Dedicated vs Hosted). Ben - want me to attach that to the MAP before we send?

Marissa
Principal Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com

Subject: Re: Post-call recap & proposed POC plan (model selection + success criteria)

Sofia / Tom,

Appreciate the quick questions. Confirming items and next steps below: 

1) Multilingual: we'll validate both Mexican and European Spanish variants via your redacted samples. Marissa recommends expanding the Spanish test set to include ~300 examples from each region to cover dialect differences. No separate model required at POC start.

2) Fallback routing: hybrid approach accepted - confidence threshold first (we'll propose threshold values after Day 4 batch run) + latency SLO fallback at 900ms. We'll add the rule-based override for "legal" and "refund" threads.

3) Data handling & residency: for the POC we will run the evaluation on Redwood Dedicated in us-west-2 and configure logs/kv-cache to write to your staging VPC via our Private connector. I'll have Laura follow up with the network checklist and the SOC2 questionnaire completion plan.

4) Cost estimate: Marissa will attach the Dedicated vs Hosted cost delta table to the MAP. Early ballpark: ~$1,200-1,600 for the 30-day Dedicated throughput baseline (depends on batching settings) vs ~$1,900-2,500 on Hosted for equivalent runs. We'll provide a precise estimate after the Day 0-3 baseline run.

Next actions & ownership:
- Globex (Sofia): share redacted sample 2k threads + 600 Spanish examples by EOD Mon 11/16.
- Redwood (Marissa): share eval script and cost delta table; add the proposed confidence threshold + latency fallback config to the MAP.
- Redwood (Laura): send the network checklist and SOC2 response timeline.
- All: confirm kickoff Wed 11/18 10:00am PT - I'll send a calendar invite once we have the MAP signed.

I'm attaching the final POC scope PDF. If you're good we'll send the MAP (DocuSign) and lock the kickoff.

Best,

Ben Carter
